welcome.heading: Welcome to Second Take
welcome.body: This is your space to build the everyday skills that make the first months after release easier. Go at your own pace. Nothing here is graded, and nothing you type leaves this device.

quizQuestions.prompt: How comfortable are you using a smartphone or computer?
quizQuestions.helper: There is no wrong answer. This just helps us pick your starting lesson.

options.label: I am brand new to it
I can do a few basics

quizQuestions.prompt: Do you have an email address you can get into today?
quizQuestions.helper: An email address is the key to most job applications and benefits sites.

options.label: No, I need to set one up
I have one but cannot get in
Yes, I can get into it

quizQuestions.prompt: When did you last hold a paid job?
quizQuestions.helper: Work history helps us decide how much resume support to show you.

options.label: I have not worked for pay before

quizQuestions.prompt: What would help you most in your first month out?
quizQuestions.helper: Pick the one that feels most urgent right now.

options.label: Getting my ID and paperwork sorted

quizQuestions.prompt: Who can you call when a day goes sideways?
quizQuestions.helper: Knowing your support list ahead of time takes pressure off later.

interviewQuestions.question: Tell me a little about yourself.
interviewQuestions.tip: Keep it to about a minute. Where you are from, what you are good at, and what kind of work you want next.
sampleAnswers: I am someone who shows up early and finishes what I start. I spent the last few years learning kitchen work and I am looking for a steady role where I can keep building on that.
I like hands-on work. I picked up maintenance and repair skills, and I am looking for a place where I can learn the rest on the job.

interviewQuestions.question: Why should we hire you for this role?
interviewQuestions.tip: Name one or two strengths and tie each to something the job actually needs.
sampleAnswers: I am reliable and I take direction well. This job needs someone who can be counted on for every shift, and that is the part I am proudest of.
I work well with a crew. I have spent years in situations where getting along with people mattered, so I do not bring drama to a team.

interviewQuestions.question: I see a gap in your work history. Can you tell me about it?
interviewQuestions.tip: Be brief and honest, then turn it forward to what you did with that time. You do not owe anyone the full story.
sampleAnswers: I was incarcerated. I used that time to finish my GED and complete a food handling certificate, and I am ready to get back to work.
I had a period away. I took classes and worked in the facility kitchen the whole time, and my references can speak to how I showed up.

interviewQuestions.question: Tell me about a time you handled a difficult situation at work.
interviewQuestions.tip: Use three steps: what happened, what you did, how it turned out.
sampleAnswers: A coworker and I disagreed about how to close up. I asked the supervisor to settle it instead of arguing on the floor, and we ended up with a written closing list everyone followed.
We were short staffed on a busy night. I took the extra station without being asked and we got through service without sending anything back.

interviewQuestions.question: What are you hoping to learn in this job?
interviewQuestions.tip: Show you want to grow. Employers like people who plan to stick around.
sampleAnswers: I would like to learn the ordering and inventory side, so over time I can take on more than my own station.
I want to get certified on the equipment here. If there is a path to a lead role, that is what I am working toward.

interviewQuestions.question: Where do you see yourself in two years?
interviewQuestions.tip: Keep it realistic and tied to this employer. Steady beats flashy.
sampleAnswers: Still here, trained up, and hopefully helping bring new people along.
In a role with more responsibility. I am not in a rush, I just want to keep moving forward.

entries.description: Lifeline takes money off your monthly phone or internet bill if you qualify. Note the Affordable Connectivity Program ended in 2024, so Lifeline is the federal program still running.

entries.title: Getting ready for your first days at work
entries.description: A work ready checklist covering what to sort out before day one and how to handle your first mistake.

entries.description: Free in person help with resumes, training programs, and local job leads. Most have computers you can use.
